cause.label: index_or_flow
cause.what_happened: SAIQ started trading 2026-10-02 after the de-SPAC with Columbus Acquisition closed on 10-01. On 10-07, its fourth session after a +260% spike on 10-05, it gapped down 18% overnight and fell another 13.5% intraday to $3.65 at 15:05 ET on 18x volume. That trading is about 0.9M shares, roughly the whole tradable float. The previous day, at 13:29 ET, the company had disclosed that SEALSQ's $10M PIPE was priced at $10.79 with a price-protection reset of up to 1,073,216 extra shares. No same-day news was found.

positioning_check: Short interest unavailable: no Nasdaq settlement yet for a ticker listed 2026-10-02, and the FINRA lag would hide any position taken during the fall anyway. No option market, so no skew. No Form 4s (foreign private issuer). Derived float: about 35k unredeemed public shares plus about 890k shares from converting 6,234,290 rights at 1/7, plus 210k representative shares whose lock-up status was not checked. WISeKey's 25M shares, the 1.5M insider shares and the about 927k PIPE shares are presumed locked (the PIPE lock-up is sourced; the others were not verified in the 424B3, which was too large to fetch). Today's roughly 0.9M shares traded is about one float turnover.

findings.finding: Most of SAIQ's tradable float is roughly 890k shares from the 1/7 conversion of 6,234,290 CAC rights, acquired at a rights-level cost basis. With only about 35k public shares left after 2,515,182 were redeemed, that holder base keeps supplying stock into 2026-10-08. After a 50% five-day slide it is plausibly but not demonstrably spent.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The rights shares became deliverable at the 2026-10-01 closing and are freely tradable, so whatever is left of that supply can sell in the 2026-10-08 session. It is undated and there is no evidence it is spent, so it sits in the window rather than later.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the four sessions since listing the stock fell 35% (10-02), rose 260% (10-05), fell 22.6% (10-06) and fell 29.3% today, so a sub-1M float swings both ways. Baseline own-falls: 1 of 4 up next day, median next close -32.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The tape trades on price. The float composition (about 96% from rights holders with near-zero cost, about 35k true public shares) appears in no document as a single number; it has to be derived from the CAC vote 8-K and the IPO description of securities. If the price held a spent seller, today's close would sit on falling volume, but volume is 18x.
findings.independence: The CAC description of securities gives the rights structure independently of the redemption count: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2028201/000101376225004333/ea023354601ex4-5_columbus.htm. Nothing independent establishes whether the supply is spent.

outside_window.finding: SEALSQ PIPE price protection: at spot $3.65, far below $10.79, the cap of 1,073,216 extra shares (more than today's whole tradable float) is effectively certain to be issued. It is measured on the 10-day VWAP ending about 2026-11-30 (60 days after the 10-01 closing).

baseline_tension: The research agrees with the volume (18x, which phase 0 ties to continuation) and the high ATR, and finds nothing dated to set against them. The name's own +260% session shows a sub-1M float can reverse violently with no news, which is why p_up sits near 50 and is not lower.
